findings.title: A removed leftover remains classified and can bypass --ignore-existing
findings.evidence: crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/retry.rs:189 — every previously classified leftover is re-added whenever its path still fails, even when the retry touched the destination and positively removed the old partial before reporting that failure.
findings.predicted_failure: If retry 1 opens the old partial, encounters a source failure, and successfully removes the partial during abort, the path is nevertheless retained as a leftover. If another process creates that destination during the wait before retry 2, retry 2 forcibly disables --ignore-existing and overwrites the newly created file, violating the requested protection and causing data loss.
findings.better_approach: Carry an explicit per-path disposition from each retry—untouched, left in place, or positively removed—and preserve prior membership only for untouched failures. Clear it after confirmed removal, and add a regression test covering removal followed by destination recreation before the next retry.
